Results.OriginalProductName: Spirit II E-310 Gas Grill (Liquid Propane)
Results.ReviewText: I've had this grill for over a month, I normally grill almost everyday, but now I do grill every day.  This grill is great, I like the clean up ability, and the overall heat transfer.  I enjoy the ease of starting the grill, you have to wait until the count of 10, before you start the grill, no whoosh when you start the grill, no singed hairs on my arms.  I've tried many different recipes on the grill, and haven't yet burned anything.  I like that the propane tank isn't inside the grill, I did put the tank on the deck and not on the hanger, easier to turn off and on.  I do like the large knobs for adjustment of the flames, and that the burners ignite in the back of the grill off a started flame.  I wish the left shelf had an option to permanently install the shelf, so when you move the grill it's got something sold to move the grill.  Overall I really enjoy the grill and it will last many years, I cover and clean the grill everyday, and I can't wait till Thanksgiving so I can grill my turkey, which I've done for almost 18 years.  Great product, and I have bought one for my daughter, she loves hers just as much, different color.
Results.Title: Great update to a grill that lasted 18 years.

Results.ReviewText: We all know it, Weber grills are the best, but not everyone can afford an $800 grill. In comes the Weber Spirit II. First off it’s built like a tank, I have no doubt this grill will last 20 years+. Second, this grill has tons of space. It is smaller than the genesis but it’s still a big grill. Third, it cooks incredibly even from corner to corner, front to back, and the flavor bars produce fantastic smoke while eliminating flare ups completely. My food tastes incredible coming off this grill. I spent less than $500 on this grill and it was worth every penny. In my opinion this is hands down the best grill for the price on the market. This grill is so far in front of any other grill in its price range you’d be a fool to purchase any other brand. No other grill can match this value, not even the Weber Genesis.

Results.ReviewText:
Looks good, nice quality, fit and finish.  Easy to assemble. Cooks food fine, as well as any other grill in the $300-$500 price range.  Primary reason I bought this for was the large wheels and folding side table as I roll my grill in and out of the garage every time I cook.  But I still have a few qualms with this grill.  #1 there is no good way to wheel thus grill around as the folding table pops out of place when using it as a handle but it's impossible to move it with the table folded down.  I may end up just bolting the table into the open position and giving up the garage space.  #2 the ignition is a little hokey and is supposed to "light the first time, every time" but I get the giant fireball every time as the spark is apparently contacting the propane stream correctly.  #3 the tool hooks aren't quite big enough to hold my spatula and brushes.  They are constantly getting bumped onto the ground.  Have to make some kind of metal hooks and cut the plastic nubs off.

If I can get some years of service of service out of it (I've only had it 6 months) I'll still be happy.  Every other brand I considered had major shortcoming; my complaints with the 310 are just annoyances.
Results.Title: Great grill for the money but...

Results.ReviewText: We received this grill as a housewarming gift. It’s the best grill I’ve ever owned. Never had a Weber before, but this grill is simple and cooks great. Also looks nice. I have not used the thermometer that connects to your cell via Bluetooth. Assembly may be difficult for some. I put it together myself but it’d go faster with two people and I reccomend reading the assembly instructions. It’s very clear step by step. Overall, we’re very pleased!

Results.ReviewText: I have had a lot of grills in my time and I have to say, this grill cooks better then anyone that I have own.  We have used it a half dozen times within the last month and every meal has turned out great.  There is only one thing that I would like to see changed.  The wheels are on the right side of the grill, so you have to pick up the left side to move it.  Well the fold down shelve is on the left, so when you want to move the grill, the shelve pops loose and wants to fold down while you are trying to move it. I suggest some kind of lock on the shelve so it can't fold down till the lock is released.  Then I would have to give it a 5 star.

Results.ReviewText: This is my 4th Weber (we move a lot and I leave my old one behind) and my biggest disappointment. I paid virtually the same price as my previous models but this model has the least to offer. No cabinet doors for storage. The grill “lid” is constructed of light material and not as solid as previous models. The propane tank visibly hangs out under the right shelf making the grill look cheap as well as making your grill deck look cheap too. The wheels are fixed so turning the grill is difficult. Thankfully it still cooks great. Finally, to move up to the next model was like a $400 upcharge which is rediculous. This could be my last Weber.
Results.Title: Less Is More

Get ready to step up your grilling experience. As the family sits down for dinner, or a couple of friends come over for a bite – this three burner grill will do its magic. With the spacious cooking area you can sear steaks on one side while grilling an appetizer on the other, and the convenient open-cart allows you to keep your tools and equipment within reach. Armed with the strong GS4 grilling system, this gas grill is sure to take you and your meals to the next level.
